answers.html:
The strongest result is an exact quantum criterion for when a predictor may discard information about the current physical system. For a specified class of interacting bosonic systems coupled to replenishing thermal baths, distinguishability from a common reference decays at a sharp rate. Each exposed measurement adds a precisely identified conditional-information term. The criterion remains valid with strong number-conserving interactions and feedback based on earlier exposed outcomes.

I also completed a positive stochastic predictor for the interacting hot-bath regime, with a finite-horizon complete-record certificate. An exact stationary example shows why its evolving conditional law matters: two systems can have the same stationary density and identical complete pooled count paths, yet have distinguishable records when the detector retains the output-port labels.

These results separate three questions that were previously intertwined:

  • What information is sufficient? The current conditional law, together with the controller and relevant detector memory.
  • When may some of that information be forgotten? When a quantitative mixing certificate makes its effect on every permitted future record small.
  • When is the retained law economical to represent? This requires additional structure. Neither positivity nor a bounded information budget supplies that conclusion by itself.

Consider mmm bosonic modes with total occupation

For an unobserved interval of duration sss,

I supplied the domain argument for simultaneous polynomial interactions: Hamiltonian cutoffs in total-number sectors, uniform number-moment tails, a trace-norm product limit, and lower semicontinuity of relative entropy. Thus the extension does not rest solely on a formal commutator calculation.

2. What measurement adds—and what the predictor must retain

Let hhh denote the exposed record so far. During the next bin, the control is selected using hhh and the retained controller state. The unread outcome cannot control the system inside that bin.

Suppose the finite-outcome instrument {Ih,y}y\{\mathcal I_{h,y}\}_y{Ih,y​}y​ averages to the stipulated unobserved controlled channel. Write

py=Tr⁡Ih,y(ρh),ρh,y=Ih,y(ρh)py,ρˉh=∑ypyρh,y.p_y=\operatorname{Tr}\mathcal I_{h,y}(\rho_h),\qquad \rho_{h,y}=\frac{\mathcal I_{h,y}(\rho_h)}{p_y}, \qquad \bar\rho_h=\sum_y p_y\rho_{h,y}.py​=TrIh,y​(ρh​),ρh,y​=py​Ih,y​(ρh​)​,ρˉ​h​=y∑​py​ρh,y​.

Then the relative-entropy chain rule gives the exact identity

∑ypyD(ρh,y∥τ)=D(ρˉh∥τ)+χh,(2)\sum_y p_yD(\rho_{h,y}\Vert\tau) = D(\bar\rho_h\Vert\tau)+\chi_h, \tag{2}y∑​py​D(ρh,y​∥τ)=D(ρˉ​h​∥τ)+χh​,(2)

where

χh=∑ypyD(ρh,y∥ρˉh)≤H(Y∣h)≤log⁡A\chi_h=\sum_y p_yD(\rho_{h,y}\Vert\bar\rho_h) \le H(Y\mid h)\le\log Aχh​=y∑​py​D(ρh,y​∥ρˉ​h​)≤H(Y∣h)≤logA

for an alphabet of size AAA.

Thus the relevant information is continually lost through mixing and replenished through conditioning on newly exposed outcomes. The distinction between unconditional stationarity and continuing conditional information acquisition is established in the literature on informational steady states; Landi, Paternostro and Belenchia explicitly develop the corresponding Holevo-information gain and loss identities. arxiv.org

Combining (1) and (2), define the actual-prefix average

Ek=EhD(ρh∥τ).\mathcal E_k = \mathbb E_h D(\rho_h\Vert\tau).Ek​=Eh​D(ρh​∥τ).

At exposed bin boundaries,

Ek≤e−κtkE0+∑j≤ke−κ(tk−tj) Eχj.(3)\boxed{ \mathcal E_k \le e^{-\kappa t_k}\mathcal E_0 + \sum_{j\le k} e^{-\kappa(t_k-t_j)} \,\mathbb E\chi_j. } \tag{3}Ek​≤e−κtk​E0​+j≤k∑​e−κ(tk​−tj​)Eχj​.​(3)

A completely explicit, less selective bound replaces Eχj\mathbb E\chi_jEχj​ by log⁡Aj\log A_jlogAj​.

For equally spaced bins of duration Δ\DeltaΔ and fixed alphabet size AAA,

Ek≤e−κkΔE0+log⁡A [1−e−κkΔ]1−e−κΔ.(4)\mathcal E_k \le e^{-\kappa k\Delta}\mathcal E_0 + \frac{\log A\,[1-e^{-\kappa k\Delta}]} {1-e^{-\kappa\Delta}}. \tag{4}Ek​≤e−κkΔE0​+1−e−κΔlogA[1−e−κkΔ]​.(4)

This is a quantitative retention principle: old conditional information receives a decaying weight, while fresh readouts contribute new information. Strong number-conserving interactions can move that information into phases and correlations without increasing this particular reference-relative quantity.

Several distinctions matter:

  • The bound concerns the average over actual record prefixes. It does not guarantee accuracy on every rare postselected outcome.
  • A bounded Ek\mathcal E_kEk​ does not bound the number of parameters, particles, tensor components or bits needed to describe ρh\rho_hρh​.
  • A stationary unconditional preparation does not imply E0=0\mathcal E_0=0E0​=0 if it is correlated with an initial controller.
  • No sparse-observation assumption is needed for (3), provided the instrument’s average channel has the stated contraction property. An additional invasive measurement channel requires its own estimate.

An operational forgetting rule

At a clean boundary, retain the actual controller and replace only the plant state in the predictor by τ\tauτ. For each prefix hhh, the complete adaptive future experiment defines a quantum-to-classical channel KhK_hKh​. Consequently,

TV⁡ ⁣(Kh(ρh),Kh(τ))≤12∥ρh−τ∥1≤D(ρh∥τ)2.\operatorname{TV}\!\left(K_h(\rho_h),K_h(\tau)\right) \le \frac12\|\rho_h-\tau\|_1 \le \sqrt{\frac{D(\rho_h\Vert\tau)}2}.TV(Kh​(ρh​),Kh​(τ))≤21​∥ρh​−τ∥1​≤2D(ρh​∥τ)​​.

Averaging,

EhTV⁡ ⁣(Kh(ρh),Kh(τ))≤Ek2.(5)\boxed{ \mathbb E_h\operatorname{TV} \!\left(K_h(\rho_h),K_h(\tau)\right) \le \sqrt{\frac{\mathcal E_k}{2}}. } \tag{5}Eh​TV(Kh​(ρh​),Kh​(τ))≤2Ek​​​.​(5)

This bounds the complete future record for any finite future horizon, using the same controller. It also bounds the joint whole-record error of a single replacement that preserves the earlier prefix probabilities.

It is a replacement inside a predictor. It does not prescribe a physical reset, and it does not make evaluation of KhK_hKh​ inexpensive.

Detector memory is part of the physical state

If an unread classical latch LLL is correlated with the plant, the relevant quantity is

∑lplD(ρl∥τ)=D(ρmarginal∥τ)+χ({pl,ρl}).(6)\sum_l p_lD(\rho_l\Vert\tau) = D(\rho_{\mathrm{marginal}}\Vert\tau) + \chi(\{p_l,\rho_l\}). \tag{6}l∑​pl​D(ρl​∥τ)=D(ρmarginal​∥τ)+χ({pl​,ρl​}).(6)

The plant marginal may equal τ\tauτ while the second term remains positive.

I retained an exact stationary Ornstein–Uhlenbeck counting example in which independently replacing the plant while preserving an unread latch changes the joint two-window record. It shows that delaying access to an outcome does not remove its correlations.

A frozen classical latch can be retained and treated componentwise through a subsequent blind interval. A latch that continues registering events receives new information. Later-accessible quantum side memory requires a separate joint contraction theorem; the unconditional entropy-power inequality used above does not supply one automatically. The counterexamples are in EXACT_LATCH_AND_RARE_RECORD_COUNTEREXAMPLES.txt.

3. Forgetting arbitrary preparation using a supplied energy bound

The stronger entropy-power inequality gives more than exponential decay from a possibly large initial relative entropy.

Let N0=Tr⁡(Nρ0)N_0=\operatorname{Tr}(N\rho_0)N0​=Tr(Nρ0​), q=e−κsq=e^{-\kappa s}q=e−κs, and suppose the actual protocol contains a genuinely blind interval of length sss. Then

D(ρs∥τn⊗m)≤Bn(s,N0):=qβ(N0−mn)−mlog⁡ ⁣[1−q+qe−g(n)].(7)\boxed{ D(\rho_s\Vert\tau_n^{\otimes m}) \le B_n(s,N_0) := q\beta(N_0-mn) - m\log\!\left[1-q+q e^{-g(n)}\right]. } \tag{7}D(ρs​∥τn⊗m​)≤Bn​(s,N0​):=qβ(N0​−mn)−mlog[1−q+qe−g(n)].​(7)

Only S(ρ0)≥0S(\rho_0)\ge0S(ρ0​)≥0 was used to eliminate the unknown preparation entropy. The bound therefore covers arbitrary finite-energy non-Gaussian and entangled preparations.

It also allows an initially correlated classical controller: apply the bound conditionally and average, retaining the controller. The energy term is linear.

Now take the hot scaling

n=νθ,θN0=E.n=\frac{\nu}{\theta}, \qquad \theta N_0=E.n=θν​,θN0​=E.

At fixed positive sss,

Bn(s,N0)⟶q(Eν−m)−mlog⁡(1−q).(8)\boxed{ B_n(s,N_0) \longrightarrow q\left(\frac E\nu-m\right)-m\log(1-q). } \tag{8}Bn​(s,N0​)⟶q(νE​−m)−mlog(1−q).​(8)

This gives an occupation-independent allowance for forgetting preparation at fixed scaled energy. It does not rely on the draining budget of a pure-loss system.

The limiting entropy allowance is asymptotically sharp over the admitted class. A coherent input with ∥αθ∥2=E/θ\|\alpha_\theta\|^2=E/\theta∥αθ​∥2=E/θ, evolved with H=0H=0H=0, becomes a displaced thermal state whose exact relative entropy tends to the right-hand side of (8). A uniformly smaller leading bound would require additional preparation or dynamical information. The subsequent Pinsker bound on record TV need not be sharp.

For a concrete exact-arithmetic check, take

m=2,n=1024,κ=1,N0≤2048,s=10.m=2,\quad n=1024,\quad \kappa=1,\quad N_0\le2048,\quad s=10.m=2,n=1024,κ=1,N0​≤2048,s=10.

Then replacement by the reference after the blind interval changes every finite future record law by at most

0.006736814.\boxed{0.006736814.}0.006736814.​

Alternatively, one ternary exposure from a reference input, followed by a blind interval of duration 101010, gives the allowance

0.004993843.\boxed{0.004993843.}0.004993843.​

These are exact-quantum preparation-replacement bounds, including admitted interactions during the blind interval. They do not include the error of a subsequent approximate simulator. The actual blind duration, bath parameters and initial energy bound remain physical resources.

The consequential remaining obstruction is economical retention under sustained observation. A finite information budget can coexist with a complicated conditional state. The present theorem supplies a safe reference replacement when its allowance is small; it does not prove that two filters forget different initializations along the same continually observed record, or that a low-dimensional family remains closed.

A broader effective theory will need to address systems without this common rapidly mixing reference—partial baths, slowly relaxing conserved quantities, spatial transport and continuously driven correlations. Those regimes require identifying which slow information must remain explicit and which fast information can be discarded with a record-level guarantee.
